scope: Four pinned code/config files plus official repository/tree/checkpoint metadata. Source inspection, not capability, sampler-law, deployment or task-harm validation.

prior_archive.difference: The ordinary OSRP consumer has a native whole-batch safe-count switch between cost minimization and reward optimization, not just reward ranking. This is a different consumer/resource fact, not a new sampling concept or evidence of harm.
prior_archive.preserved_negatives: Prior strong-CEM, TD-MPC2 Q-only, higher-order parity and Cosmos K8 negative gates remain unchanged; none are reopened by changing seeds.

native_call_path.finding: Encode actual observation; RSSM posterior consumes actual previous action. Evaluation selects configured planner output.
CCE draws actor proposals if mixture>0 and Gaussian bounded actions inside WM imagine; warm-starts action_mean and runs configured iterations.
imagine scans H RSSM transitions, keeps initial plus H states, and calls policy between transitions.
Score rewards/costs, choose elites, update mean/std, return mean[0].

osrp_vector.configuration_inheritance: No local planner override: defaults at configs.yaml:111 imply mixture_coef .05 and remaining planner values.
osrp_vector.cost_statistic: Decoder observation.mode() uses hazard coordinates9:25 as eight 2D hazard positions. Each returned frame counts 0..8 hazards with distance<=.25; traj_cost sums this count across the initial state plus H predicted states (H+1 frames). This is a nonnegative geometric collision-count proxy, not a Monte Carlo average or quantile.
osrp_vector.decisive_source_implication: For the published config, traj_cost>=0 and the predicate is traj_cost<0. Therefore num_safe_traj=0 and the <50 branch always chooses by -cost; the proposed safe-count mode switch is unreachable.
osrp_vector.decision: No-Go for the targeted safety-mode-switch mechanism on the small published OSRP-Vector configuration. This is not a Clean failure or a general SafeDreamer exclusion.

osrp.cost_statistic: Greedy defines costfn=wm.heads[cost](s).mean()[1:] at behaviors.py:40-42. CCE uses cost.sum(0)*(1000/H) at369-374, not the bootstrapped cost_ret it also receives. The configured cost head is signed symlog_disc with bins on (-20,20); its decoded mean is not guaranteed nonnegative. Thus the Vector nonnegative-cost/strict-zero-threshold argument must not be applied to this learned cost head.
osrp.gate: Count C_i<2. If fewer than50, rank all candidates by -C_i; otherwise rank safe-indexed candidates by reward return. Not a per-candidate chance constraint, particle quantile or confidence bound.
osrp.decision: A genuine native stochastic learned-forecast safety consumer is present in source; permission isolation and local matched Clean/actual cost are unqualified. No experiment accepted here.

osrp_lag.gate: Same whole-batch count rule; reward-side ranking uses ret[0]-state[lagrange_penalty]*cost_ret[0]. This is a separate native variant, not a changed Vector threshold.
osrp_lag.cost_statistic: Uses the same signed symlog_disc(-20,20) cost head and single-trajectory time sum scaled by1000/H; cost-head means are not guaranteed nonnegative. The Vector strict-zero-threshold exclusion does not apply.

bsrp_lag.finding: expl_behavior=None; not the online CCE consumer screened here.

stochasticity.law: RSSM draws a batched factorized categorical (or diagonal-normal alternative) state via dist.sample(seed=nj.rng()) at each imagined step. A shared PRNG key argument is not itself shared candidate noise; no candidate-broadcast random variable is shown in inspected code.
stochasticity.limits: OneHotDist implementation, Ninjax key splitting and actual loaded distribution were not executed or separately source-audited. Independence is the standard batched-distribution interpretation, not an empirical independence test. Given a fixed initial sampled posterior, future branch draws are per-batch-element; initial posterior uncertainty is shared through replicated latent.
stochasticity.complete_law_requirement: Preserve each candidate full temporal and cross-coordinate forecast law conditioned on its own initial latent and fixed action sequence. Preserving one-step marginals or head means is insufficient.

permission_boundary.native: Internal in-process RSSM distribution sampler; no external per-candidate noise, seed or forecast service interface established in these four files.
permission_boundary.global_rng_is_not_valid_restricted_contr: nj.rng() also supplies actor/Gaussian proposals and posterior sampling. Replacing a global seed changes trusted candidate actions or initial belief.
permission_boundary.added_setting: A narrowly scoped supply-chain/runtime hook inside imagined RSSM draws could be defined as a research threat model; it would be added and must exclude posterior/proposal RNG, heads, weights, costs, thresholds and actual controls.
permission_boundary.adaptation_boundary: Keeping the initial candidate set fixed is possible for a bounded first-iteration diagnostic. Native later CEM means/proposals depend on selected elites, so an entire unchanged candidate bank across all iterations is not automatically a native closed-loop comparison.

resources.vector_command: python SafeDreamer/train.py --configs osrp_vector --method osrp --run.script eval_only --run.from_checkpoint /path/checkpoint.ckpt --task safetygymcoor_SafetyPointGoal1-v0 --jax.platform cpu --run.steps 10000
resources.measurement: Sizes and LFS hashes are official HF metadata only, not downloaded or independently hashed weights. Each vector checkpoint is26,564,352 bytes; ordinary matched OSRP PointGoal1 is391,867,080 bytes.
resources.stated_runtime: README describes Python3.8/JAX0.3.25, matching jaxlib and Safety-Gymnasium; CPU evaluation documented. Local installation, weight strict-load, environment assets, physical cost recording and Clean performance are untested.
resources.entrypoint_limit: The four-file bound excludes train.py/eval_only.py/env adapter. No claim that unseen entry-point overrides were audited; official README command has no explicit cost_limit override.

minimal_next_decision: Do not download the small Vector checkpoint for the proposed safety-count-switch study. Ordinary OSRP is only a conditional resource lead: first rule out source-level gating/indexing artifacts, define a genuinely restricted imagined-noise interface, then qualify one unchanged native Clean task and a frozen same-candidate comparison with independent real Safety-Gymnasium cost. There is no selected or frozen attack pilot from this screen.
novelty_limits: Changing only cross-candidate dependence is an existing sampling/coupling idea. A different safe-count consumer is not enough for a new paper: any claim must isolate actual safety-cost effects beyond generic multiple-selection/CRN effects and the identified indexing issue, with explicit added permissions and truthful negative controls. Also separate any effect from unvalidated elite-mean execution, since constituent candidate costs do not certify an averaged action.

implementation_caveats.finding: The safe branch uses fixed-size jnp.nonzero(mask,size=mask.size) with no explicit valid-count masking or custom fill value. Default zero-index padding can admit/repeat candidate0 if it is unsafe. This is a general indexing issue to qualify before attributing unsafe selection to a new coupling mechanism; no operator or task test was performed here.

Native CCE averages elite action trajectories, blends the previous mean by momentum, and executes mean[0]. The inspected policy does not separately forecast/score that resulting aggregate action before execution. Safe constituent trajectory labels therefore do not certify the executed mean. This is an ordinary nonconvex planning/aggregation confound, not evidence for a new coupling mechanism.
